source.title: Belfast Telegraph, 2 June 1967, p. 8 ("Sion tops the poll: rural elections with 96 pc"); Belfast News-Letter, 2 June 1967, p. 2 ("Poll surprises in many areas")
source.publisher: Belfast Telegraph (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: Read on the page images (council-audit, Nov 2026): Belfast Telegraph, 2 June 1967, p. 8 'Joseph C. McLaughlin (Ind.) 87; Patrick J. McLaughlin (Ind.) 36; Laurence Brolly (Ind.) 36. Maj. 31. Electorate 206. Total poll 179. Spoiled votes none'; the News-Letter, 2 June 1967, p. 2 prints the same figures with (Nat.) labels.

note: Triennial election, polled Thursday 1 June 1967. Four divisions were contested in the results printed; Scriggan, listed as a contest at nomination, does not appear in the result reports and is not recorded. McLaughlin elected; 86.8 pc poll; valid poll 179. Both papers print P. J. McLaughlin's vote as 36, but the printed majority (31) and total poll (179, no spoiled votes) both give 56, which is kept.
correctionNote: Corrected from the page image of the Belfast Telegraph, 2 June 1967, p. 8 (council-audit, Nov 2026): the two McLaughlins as printed (were 'McLoughlin'), Laurence Brolly as printed (was Lawrence), and the printed electorate, total poll, spoiled votes and majority recorded; P. J. McLaughlin's 56 kept against the papers' misprinted 36 because the majority and poll prove it.
